one_liner: Training-free dynamic column-sparse attention and MLP kernels for diffusion transformers; about 2.16x end-to-end on HunyuanVideo over torch.compile'd dense.
what_it_does: Chipmunk speeds up diffusion-transformer (DiT) inference (HunyuanVideo, Wan2.1, FLUX.1-dev, Mochi) by reusing each layer's attention and MLP outputs from the previous denoising step and recomputing only a sparse delta. It is a PyTorch package, not a kernel library with a stable C++ API: you load a global YAML config (chipmunk.util.config.load_from_file) and replace your attention call with a SparseDiffAttn module and optionally your MLP with SparseDiffMLP, then patchify or voxelize tokens in the model's forward. The custom kernels (csp_attn, dense_attn, dense_colsum_attn, csp_mlp_mm1, csp_mlp_mm2_and_scatter_add and indexed-IO helpers) are exposed as a torch extension under chipmunk.cuda / torch.ops.chipmunk.
how_it_is_fast: Activations change slowly across diffusion steps and attention and MLP activations are sparse, so on a dense 'full step' it records each query group's top keys (column sums of attention, via dense_colsum_attn) and a cached output, and on later steps computes only the contribution of those keys/neurons as a delta added to the cache. The sparsity is laid out as [192, 1] column-sparse chunks for attention and [128, 1] for the MLP, so producer warps gather the needed K/V columns into dense shared-memory tiles and the tensor-core GEMMs stay dense; kernels are written in ThunderKittens for Hopper (TMA, cp.async.reduce.bulk for the cache scatter-add). Tokens are reordered into patches or 4x6x8 voxels so neighbouring queries share one sparsity pattern, and dense steps are injected on a schedule to limit drift.
when_to_use: Batch-1 text-to-video or text-to-image DiT inference on H100 (Hopper) where attention dominates, e.g. HunyuanVideo 720x1280x129, where Chipmunk alone cut 1030 s to 477 s
You already use one of the four integrated models (HunyuanVideo, Wan2.1, FLUX.1-dev, Mochi) and can run the shipped example scripts and configs
You accept a small, measurable quality change (the README reports VBench, ImageReward, GenEval and CLIP scores per setting) in exchange for latency
You want to stack sparsity with step caching (TeaCache-style) or sliding-tile attention (STA), which the README combines for 2.5-3.7x end-to-end
Ampere GPUs, via the Triton ports, if you accept that the README gives no separate Ampere numbers beyond 'comparable E2E generation speedup'
when_not_to_use: You need exact attention or MLP outputs: this is lossy approximate computation, not a drop-in replacement for FlashAttention-3 or cuBLAS
LLM serving, training, causal attention or head dims other than 128: dense_attn is non-causal with 128-dim heads, and the method relies on the multi-step denoising loop
Batched generation: SparseDiffMLP asserts input shape (1, N, C) and the static masks are built for batch 1
You only need the headline 3.7x on HunyuanVideo: step caching alone (TeaCache) reaches 3.69x, so most of that number is not Chipmunk
Production use needing support: stale since 2025-09-08, open unanswered issues on flickering (Wan 14B I2V on A100) and OOM (Wan2.1-14B on A100 80GB with 120 GB host RAM)

integration.form: module (Python package with a torch CUDAExtension built by pip install -e . --no-build-isolation)
integration.dependencies: PyTorch >= 2.5, ThunderKittens (git submodule), Triton, flash_attn, CUDA libraries (cuda, cublas, cudart, cudadevrt), plus diffusers, transformers, einops, ray and other packages in requirements.txt
integration.min_toolchain: CUDA Toolkit >= 12.4 (12.8 recommended), nvcc -std=c++20, Python 3.11 in the quickstart; built with -O3 --use_fast_math
integration.platforms: NVIDIA Hopper (sm_90a) for the CUDA attention and MLP kernels; other generations (Ampere tested) fall back to Triton ports, with copy_indices, topk_indices and mask_to_indices compiled for all; Linux with conda in the docs
integration.thread_safety: not documented; configuration is a process-global GLOBAL_CONFIG dict and the static attention masks are module-level singletons, so treat it as one model per process
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — SparseDiffAttn replaces an F.scaled_dot_product_attention call with the same (q, k, v) signature, but it needs a global config, a LayerCounter per layer and per-step state, and returns approximate outputs

gotchas: The first one or two generations are slower because of torch.compile cold starts; the README says speedups appear from generation 3
Pinned-CPU-memory offloading of caches and indices can take up to ~5 minutes at model initialization and can exhaust host RAM (issue #6 needed offloading disabled and a smaller LARGE_BUF_SIZE)
SparseDiffMLP requires the activation to be a GELU module because the kernel fuses bias, GELU and cache subtraction
Multi-GPU is supported only for HunyuanVideo, on a separate multigpu branch with its own Dockerfile
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Chipmunk over FlashAttention-3 or SageAttention only for H100 diffusion-transformer inference where a small quality change is acceptable, since it skips work rather than computing exact (FA3) or quantized-but-dense (SageAttention) attention; for anything else, including LLMs, those two are drop-in and model-agnostic. It is built on ThunderKittens, which remains the choice for dense Hopper kernels.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README numbers on H100: HunyuanVideo 720x1280x129 at 50 steps drops from 1030 s (torch.compile'd reference repo) to 477 s with Chipmunk alone (2.16x) and to 277 s with step caching (3.72x, vs 3.69x for TeaCache alone); FLUX.1-dev 768x1280 goes from 6.60 s to 4.90 s (1.41x). The layer-level claims (attention 9.3x over FlashAttention-3, MLP 2.5x over torch-compiled nn.Sequential) come from a chart with no stated sparsity level, shapes or script, and the repo's only timing code is commented out and compares against torch SDPA.
status_note: Stale (last commit 2025-09-08) research code from Together AI, Hazy Research and Sandy Research; MIT-licensed so the kernels can be copied, but expect to own the integration and the open quality and memory issues yourself.
